children: Core & Main
shares fell as much as 6.2% to a two-year low Wednesday as investors focused on sluggish underlying demand and sales growth that relied partly on acquisitions.

The stock is down about 20% this year, despite the water infrastructure distributor reporting fiscal second-quarter earnings that exceeded Wall Street expectations. Revenue barely topped the consensus estimate while management merely reaffirmed its full-year outlook.

For investors, the report showed a split market. Municipal spending, fire protection projects and construction of treatment plants and data centers supported demand. Data centers require substantial water infrastructure for cooling and fire suppression. Still, weakness in storm drainage and other construction-sensitive markets restrained broader growth.

The most troubling detail was that six-month revenue increased only 1.3% and the gain came primarily from acquisitions. Storm drainage sales declined during that period because of lower volume. That suggests the underlying business remains soft even as Core & Main
spends money to add locations and acquired operations.

Gross margin also slipped to 26.7% in the quarter from 26.8% a year earlier. The decline was small, but it gave investors another reason to question how quickly stronger project activity will translate into faster profit growth. The company described the current demand environment as “mixed.”
Quarterly results beat estimates
Revenue rose 2.5% to $2.145 billion from $2.093 billion a year earlier. That narrowly beat the Wall Street consensus estimate of $2.14 billion.
Adjusted earnings rose 8% to $0.94 a share from $0.87 to beat analysts’ estimate of $0.86.
Net income rose to $150 million, or $0.77 a share, from $141 million, or $0.70 a share.
Earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, adjusted for certain items, increased 3% to $274 million. The adjusted ebitda margin edged up to 12.8% from about 12.7%.

Operating income increased 6.6% to $227 million. Selling, general and administrative expenses declined slightly to $301 million as cost reductions and lower incentive compensation offset higher distribution expenses and investments in new locations and sales initiatives.
Acquisitions prop up growth

Sales of pipes, valves and fittings increased because of acquisitions rather than clearly identified organic growth. Quarterly storm drainage sales were essentially unchanged. Fire protection revenue benefited from higher volume and prices while smart utility product sales rose mainly because of pricing.
Those categories include the pipes, fittings, valves, meters, hydrants, storm drains and fire protection equipment used by municipalities, private water systems and contractors.
“Municipal demand remained a source of strength,” Chief Executive Mark Witkowski said in the earnings announcement.
Large capital projects, including water treatment plants and data centers, also delivered strong growth. Core & Main
opened seven new locations during fiscal 2026, including two during and shortly after the quarter.
Outlook offers little new fuel
Core & Main
reaffirmed its fiscal 2026 forecast for revenue of $7.8 billion to $7.9 billion, representing growth of 2% to 3%.
Management continues to forecast adjusted ebitda of $950 million to $980 million with a margin of 12.2% to 12.4%. Core & Main
didn’t provide adjusted earnings-per-share guidance in the release.

The distributor repurchased $169 million of stock during the quarter and another $11 million after the quarter ended. Year-to-date repurchases totaled nearly $270 million. Even that support failed to reassure investors looking for stronger organic sales growth and a more decisive improvement in demand.

title: Core & Main slides to 2-yr low on concerns about organic growth
